tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand AutoSort+'s purpose: a Thunderbird browser extension that automatically categorizes and sorts emails using AI. The README covers features (multi-provider AI support, batch processing, i18n), installation, quick start, and the system architecture overview. This gives you the vocabulary and context for every component explored next.

tour.title: Extension Manifest
tour.description: The manifest.json declares this as a WebExtension (manifest v2) targeting Thunderbird 78+. It defines the permissions needed (messagesRead, messagesModify, messagesMove, storage, menus, tabs), registers the background scripts (logger.js then background.js), the options page (options.html), and internationalization via default_locale. This file is the blueprint of the entire extension -- every other file is wired in here.

tour.title: Core Email Sorting Engine
tour.description: background.js is the extension's service worker and the most connected file in the project (fanOut=35). It implements the core email analysis, classification, and auto-sort engine. It depends on three js/ modules (providers-config, tab-fetch-utils, ollama) to perform LLM API calls. Key functions include analyzeEmailContent for AI-powered email classification, batchAnalyzeEmails for processing multiple emails with concurrency control, and classifyAndMove for applying the sort decision. This is the heart of the extension.

tour.title: LLM Provider Configuration
tour.description: providers-config.js defines the supported LLM providers (Gemini, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible) with their batch sizes, context windows, and metadata. It provides validation and lookup helpers that background.js uses to determine how to call each provider's API. Understanding this module explains how the extension switches between cloud (Gemini) and local (Ollama) AI backends.

tour.title: CORS-Workaround Tab Fetching
tour.description: tab-fetch-utils.js implements a clever pattern: creating hidden browser tabs to bypass CORS restrictions when calling LLM APIs from the extension's background script. It provides generic fetchViaTab plus provider-specific wrappers (ollamaChatViaTabUtil, openaiCompatChatViaTabUtil). This is why the extension needs the 'tabs' permission from Step 2's manifest and how it communicates with external AI services without a server proxy.
tour.languageLesson: Browser extensions run in a restricted environment. Using hidden tabs to make fetch calls bypasses CORS because the tab loads a regular web page context, not the extension's privileged context. The background script controls these tabs programmatically via the WebExtension tabs API.

tour.title: Ollama Client and Worker
tour.description: The ollama.js module provides the Ollama client class that normalizes the host URL and exposes the base configuration for local LLM API communication. The ollama-worker.js wraps this client in a Web Worker to offload API calls to a background thread, preventing UI blocking during analysis. Together they enable the local AI sorting mode as an alternative to cloud-based Gemini.

tour.title: Key Background Functions
tour.description: Building on the modules from Steps 4-6, these core functions in background.js implement the email sorting pipeline: extractEmailContext pulls email content and uses extractTextFromParts to handle MIME multipart emails; analyzeEmailContent sends the content to the configured LLM provider and checks Gemini rate limits via checkAndTrackGeminiRateLimit; applyLabelsToMessages moves emails to the classified folders; and storeMoveHistory tracks the last 100 moves for the user to review.

tour.title: Settings UI and Translations
tour.description: options.js powers the settings page (options.html) where users configure their AI provider, API keys, folder mappings, and other preferences. It depends on i18n.js for internationalized labels, providers-config.js for provider metadata, and tab-fetch-utils.js for testing API key connectivity. The escapeHtml helper prevents XSS in user-entered configuration values. This is where users spend most of their setup time.

tour.title: Internationalization System
tour.description: The i18n module (js/i18n.js) provides applyTranslations, which scans the DOM for data-i18n attributes and replaces them with localized strings from the browser's i18n API. The actual message strings live in the locale config files (_locales/en/messages.json for English and _locales/zh_CN/messages.json for Chinese). This system powers the multi-language support mentioned in Step 1's README.
tour.languageLesson: Browser extensions use the chrome.i18n.getMessage() API with __MSG_key__ placeholders in HTML/manifest. The i18n.js module extends this by processing data-i18n attributes at runtime, allowing dynamic translation of the options page without reloading.

tour.title: Debug Logger
tour.description: logger.js provides the DebugLogger class with tagged, color-coded console logging and a queue-based buffer. When debug mode is off, log messages are queued; when enabled, the buffer flushes. The content.js script initializes this logger and listens for storage changes to toggle logging at runtime. This utility is loaded first in the manifest's background scripts array, making it available to all other background code.

tour.title: Ollama Integration Setup
tour.description: OLLAMA_SETUP.md documents how to configure the local Ollama AI provider as an alternative to cloud-based Gemini. This complements the ollama.js client (Step 6) and the ollama-popup.js UI. Understanding this file explains the extension's offline-capable architecture -- users can run their own LLM locally without sending email content to any external service.

tour.title: Auto-Sort Test Validation
tour.description: test-auto-sort.test.js validates the auto-sort storage migration fix, comparing before/after behavior of handleNewMailCheck and getAutoSortValue. This test file serves as a concrete example of how the extension's settings persistence works and provides a regression safety net for the auto-sort feature that drives the core functionality from Step 3.
